thread:
Maya Chen: Heads up — after the sidecar prefetch change this morning a couple of dashboards are showing rows from the wrong tenant. Not a full leak but quicklinks sometimes surface another org's snippets.

Jordan Lee: ugh. repro steps? which dashboards / quicklinks?

Maya Chen: repro steps: 1) open Insights -> dashboard A 2) click quicklink to panel 3) observe list shows rows with org_id=1234 even though my session org is 5678. Happens ~30% of cold prefetches.

Samir Patel: do you have an http trace? could be header not being forwarded by sidecar prefetch worker.

Maya Chen: pasted snippet: 
```
GET /internal/prefetch?panel=abc
X-Redwood-Org: 5678
...\n200 OK
{"rows": [..., {"org_id": 1234, "snippet": "..."} ]}
```

Kevin Ortiz: that response org_id mismatch implies either stale cache on the prefetcher or upstream routing landed on a backend serving tenant 1234. We changed affinity routing last week — could be an edge-case.

Jordan Lee: rollout-bot says the prefetch sidecar was rolled to canary at 09:12 and to 50% at 09:40. deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-20T09:40 by @release-captain.

Maya Chen: repro was at 09:53 after 50% roll. Seems correlated.

Samir Patel: hypothesis: prefetch service reads org from `req.cookies.session` fallback if header missing. Canary sidecars might be reading a cached session store that has stale mapping when under load.

Jordan Lee: simple mitigation: short-circuit prefetch to require explicit `X-Redwood-Org` header and reject if absent. We can return 409 so UI falls back to on-demand fetch (slower but safe). Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Kevin Ortiz: safe. But we need telemetry to detect frequency before flip. Add a counter like `prefetch.org_mismatch{expected,observed}` and a histogram for latency. Grafana link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd/prefetch?org=1

Maya Chen: +1 on counter. Also we should add an internal contract check in the prefetch internal API: if resp.org != req.org then drop and log with trace id. Quick snippet: 
```
if (resp.orgId !== req.headers['x-redwood-org']) {
  log.warn(`org_mismatch ${req.id} got=${resp.orgId} expected=${req.headers['x-redwood-org']}`)
  return 409
}
```

Samir Patel: debate: that check is correct but adds work on the critical path. If we run it only on canary mode it might be fine. Alternative: make it sampling-only + metric and do reject after threshold.

Jordan Lee: agree sampling first. Add a canary-only assertion that flips to strict rejection if metric > 0.5% of prefetches. I'll sketch a PR.

Kevin Ortiz: also need to audit router affinity config — I suspect older prefetch pods are being sticky to different instance pools that serve mixed tenants. I'll open an ops ticket to validate route table.

Maya Chen: action items: 1) Jordan will open PR for sampling + metric (assign Jordan) 2) Kevin will validate affinity table + canary distribution 3) Samir will add temporary dashboard panels and a perf check 4) I will throttle prefetch to 10 rps per user as quick mitigation.

Jordan Lee: I'll cut the PR and add unit tests for org-assertion. Will tag @Samir for telemetry events.

deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-20T10:15 - prefetch service paused at 50% (manual pause).

grafana-bot: alert created: `prefetch_org_mismatch_rate > 0.1%` -> channel #incidents if fires.

Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll keep the thread updated with traces. If someone sees more cross-tenant rows drop me a line with trace id. :pray:
